reasons.A: Short-to-medium declarative sentences with plain joins and a dry, understated irony that lands in brief closing sentences, like the passage; period touches such as 'To-morrow' fit without overdoing it.
reasons.C: Period register and ironic stance are close, but the rhetorical question, balanced semicolon antitheses and polished epigram endings are more essayistic and more wit-forward than the passage's plain reportage.
reasons.B: Longer, list-heavy sentences with accumulating appositives and an earnest, explanatory close; less of the passage's dry irony and clipped rhythm, and a more modern feel ('Tomorrow', 'go West').
